slides.heading: Quick Sort
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Sorting
slides.narration: Let's solve Quick Sort, a hard sorting problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: In-place quicksort, recursing into the smaller partition first to bound stack depth.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. In-place quicksort, recursing into the smaller partition first to bound stack depth.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Partition around a pivot so smaller values go left and larger right, then sort each side.
slides.narration: Partition around a pivot so smaller values go left and larger right, then sort each side.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Quick sort → O(n log n) average, O(log n) stack
slides.narration: Quadratic sorts compare everything. Quick sort partitions around a pivot and recurses, n log n on average.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 3. Recurse into the smaller side first
4. Loop on the larger to bound the stack
slides.narration: Step by step. First, pick a pivot. Second, partition with two pointers. Third, recurse into the smaller side first. Fourth, loop on the larger to bound the stack.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Sort loops while lo is below hi: partition, place the pivot at r, recurse on the smaller side and loop on the larger.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(n log n) avg, O(n^2) worst
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n avg, O of n squared worst. Space is O of log n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Worst case O(n²) on sorted input → random pivot
Recurse smaller side to bound stack
slides.narration: Sorted input with a first-element pivot is quadratic; randomise. Recurse into the smaller side first to keep the stack logarithmic.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Three-way partitioning handles many duplicates well.
